title: Why search in the forest
hookLine: kaahe re ban khojan jaaee: why look in the forest; He is within, like scent in a flower (Dhanasri M9, ang 684)

lines: SEEKERS WHO LEFT FOR THE FOREST.
cards: You're late, and you can't find your glasses. Kitchen counter, coat pocket, under the sofa cushions, the car. You ask everyone in the house.
Ten minutes of rising panic. Then you catch yourself in the hallway mirror, and there they are, pushed up on top of your head. The thing you were hunting for was with you the whole time.
Guru Tegh Bahadur's hymn in Raag Dhanasri begins with a gentle question for a seeker setting out for the forest, to look for God far from ordinary life.

teach.b: The hymn opens kaahe re ban khojan jaaee. Why go searching in the forest? Ban is forest; khojan is to search.
Then, in paraphrase: the One who dwells in everything, and is always untouched, is with you, absorbed in you. And two pictures.

As fragrance lives inside a flower, and as a reflection lives inside a mirror, so the Lord lives within, without a break. Search within your own heart, brother. You can't see a flower's scent, or pull it out and hold it.
But it's in every petal, and the moment you lean close, it's there.
And the face in the mirror isn't somewhere else, waiting to be found. It appears exactly where you're looking.

Then the hymn adds, in paraphrase: know the One as the same, outside and inside; this is the wisdom the Guru has taught. So it isn't saying God is only inside and the world is empty. Inside and outside are one presence.
And the last line: says Nanak, without knowing your own self, the moss of doubt is not cleared away. Kaaee is the green moss that grows on still water and hides it.
Sikh teaching keeps the search inside ordinary life, the householder's life of work and family. The hymn doesn't condemn the forest.
It just says the One is already here, like the scent in the flower you're holding.

how: Guru Tegh Bahadur's Dhanasri shabad 'kaahe re ban khojan jaaee' is sung in kirtan; Sikhs often cite its images of the flower's scent and the mirror's reflection for the teaching that God is found within ordinary life.

o: a reflection in a polished mirror
a forest where seekers go to search
fragrance, the scent inside a flower

games.q: why search in the forest — tap the pairs.

s: the hymn says God is only inside, and the world is empty
it says know the One as the same, outside and inside.
the hymn compares the Lord within to scent in a flower
and to a reflection in a mirror.
the hymn ends saying doubt clears without knowing yourself
without knowing your own self, it says, the moss of doubt isn't cleared.

games.q: you're ready to leave home for the forest to find God. what does the Dhanasri hymn ask?
o: why go searching in the forest?
games.why: kaahe re ban khojan jaaee: why go searching in the forest? the Lord lives within, like scent in a flower and a face in a mirror.

practice: Bring something fragrant close, a flower, a herb, a piece of fruit, a cup of tea, and breathe in slowly, noticing that the scent is invisible and everywhere in it; if nothing's near, remember a smell you love, rain on dust, bread, a rose.
Then sit with the hymn's idea that what you're looking for may be this close. If you pray, you can rest in Waheguru between breaths.

wordCard.voice: Baas, fragrance. Guru Tegh Bahadur's Dhanasri hymn says the Lord lives within, like baas in a flower and a face in a mirror.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: baas, fragrance. The hymn says the Lord lives within as baas lives in a flower.

carryVoice: Your line: scent in the flower. Peace isn't only after the trip or the move; it can be right where you are. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Raag Dhanasri, Mahalla 9, 'kaahe re ban khojan jaaee' (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 684)
